clue.text: Diabolically meaningful work of 4 29, whence eight other clues

definitions.text: Diabolically meaningful work of 4 29, whence eight other clues

parts.words: Diabolically meaningful work of 4 29, whence eight other clues
parts.note: a book of definitions with a wicked twist, written by the American at 4/29, from which eight clues in this grid are lifted word for word

explanation.surface: A note pointing the solver to a satirical book by a famous American wit, the source of several clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight clues (ALONE, PLAN, HISTORIAN, POSITIVE, LAWYER, PIANO, BORE, CONVENT) are entries copied from this book, so each is a cryptic definition in its author's sardonic voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bierce's satirical lexicon gives cynical meanings to ordinary words, so its definitions are literally devilish.

clue.text: Low grades given to drink in final test, perhaps

parts.note: D and E are low marks on a school grading scale
cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Poor marks handed out to someone drinking during the last exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding match or game settles a contest, like a closing examination, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Tax I cut initially, looking to future

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word cut

explanation.surface: Someone forecasting the future who trimmed their tax bill at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatic means prophetic, describing one who foresees what is coming.

clue.text: Star in club mixing drinks?

indicators.note: mixing tells us the letters of star, in and club are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity at a nightclub shaking up cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags slang: alcohol oils the wheels of conversation, so drinks get called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang treats alcohol as something that oils social conversation, a jocular synonym.

clue.text: Eccentric American, a doctor, got up last stand at church

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
rose means got up, past tense of rise
a bier is the stand on which a coffin rests, the last one anyone needs
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An odd American physician stood up for the final time in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last stand' suggests a final defence, but it is the coffin stand. Ambrose Bierce was a sardonic American writer who vanished in Mexico in 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: Bierce was a notoriously cynical, idiosyncratic US journalist and author, so eccentric fits.

clue.text: A Conservative minister's aide? That's right

parts.note: a curate assists a parish minister or vicar

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Tory cleric's assistant is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and right are synonyms meaning correct.

clue.text: Boxing match — outside ring, however

indicators.note: outside says the word for however is placed around the ring letter

parts.note: but can mean however
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boxing fight held outdoors rather than in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a single contest in boxing or wrestling.

clue.text: Taking a break from M R P performing with jazz HA IE singer

parts.note: an actor on stage is said to be on
Billie Holiday was a celebrated jazz singer

explanation.surface: Resting from performing with a jazz singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray letters in the clue as held are OCR noise from the page; the wordplay is performing (ON) plus the jazz singer Billie HOLIDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away from work on vacation is resting from duties.

clue.text: Stretch of river MART N C containing vessels

indicators.note: containing says the river's name holds the vessels inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of river with boats on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats on the river, but here they are kitchen pans. The stray letters in the clue as held are OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch of land, water or sky.

clue.text: In bad company

parts.note: a cynic's view that one's own self is the worst companion of all

explanation.definitionFit: Being solitary means having only oneself for company, which Bierce mocks as poor company.

clue.text: Husband of Catholic becomes a bishop in kind of conversion

indicators.note: becomes signals that one letter of the word is swapped for others

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A Catholic man's spouse is consecrated as a bishop during a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion' suggests a change of faith, but it is the metabolic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Catabolic describes metabolism breaking complex molecules down, a biochemical change of substances.

clue.text: Joint on a Parisian square

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means the joint's word comes after

parts.note: un is French for a
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A cannabis cigarette on a Paris square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'square' paint a drug scene in a French plaza; square here means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone square is conventional and out of touch, the opposite of fashionable.

clue.text: See 1
Bother about the best method of accomplishing an accidental result

definitions.text: Bother about the best method of accomplishing an accidental result

parts.words: Bother about the best method of accomplishing an accidental result
parts.note: a cynic's verb for scheming in advance when outcomes come about by chance anyway

explanation.definitionFit: To devise a scheme is to work out how to achieve something, which Bierce says happens by luck regardless.

clue.text: Draw plan I twice revised for city in East

indicators.note: revised says the letters of draw, plan and the doubled I are reordered
twice means the letter I is used two times

explanation.surface: An instruction to redraw a map of an eastern city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawalpindi is a major city in Pakistan, in the East from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Subject to fire again in square he attacks

annotationWithheld.why: 'Subject to fire again in square he attacks': RE + HEAT or RE(HE)AT, but no reading of 'square' gives the needed letters; likely an OCR misread with no scan to check
annotationWithheld.clue: Subject to fire again in square he attacks

clue.text: A broad-gauge gossip

parts.note: railway imagery for someone who spreads tittle-tattle on a grand scale about the past

explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler of the past reports on people's doings, which Bierce mocks as wide-ranging tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Get ready to play cello? Fine instrument will sound

indicators.note: sound at the end tells us the preceding phrase is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: a Strad, a Stradivarius violin family instrument, plus will contracted to 'll

explanation.surface: Preparing for a cello performance, promising a superb instrument will be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: A cellist sits with the instrument between the legs, hence the question mark. 'Strad'll' said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astride something with legs either side is how a cellist holds the instrument.

clue.text: Palm seed in white loaf

parts.note: ivory is a creamy white colour
loaf and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: A palm seed found in a white bread loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The ivory nut is the hard seed of a South American palm, used as vegetable ivory for buttons.

clue.text: Mistaken at the top of one's voice

definitions.text: Mistaken at the top of one's voice

parts.words: Mistaken at the top of one's voice
parts.note: a cynic's view of someone utterly sure of themselves, loudly wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Being certain or sure, Bierce suggests, usually means being wrong but loud about it.

clue.text: Parking car, is tragical running over old pedestrian

indicators.note: running over puts the scrambled letters around the old letter
tragical suggests a disaster that wrecks the order of car and is

explanation.surface: In a car park, a tragic accident in which a car runs over an elderly pedestrian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like the accident victim but means dull, and 'tragical' is the anagram signal for CAR IS, making RSAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian and prosaic are synonyms meaning dull and unimaginative.

clue.text: One skilled in circumvention of the law

definitions.text: One skilled in circumvention of the law

parts.words: One skilled in circumvention of the law
parts.note: a cynic's view of legal professionals as experts at getting round statutes

explanation.definitionFit: A legal practitioner, Bierce jibes, is paid to find ways around rules rather than uphold them.

clue.text: Stop English city overturning new layout

parts.note: rest means stop

indicators.note: in a down entry overturning means the city's name is read upwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Halting an English city's plan to overturn its new design.
explanation.definitionFit: A restyle is a fresh design or arrangement replacing the old one.

clue.text: A parlour utensil for subduing the impenitent visitor

definitions.text: A parlour utensil for subduing the impenitent visitor

parts.words: A parlour utensil for subduing the impenitent visitor
parts.note: a cynic's view of a drawing-room instrument played to drive away guests who overstay

explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument in the sitting room, Bierce jokes, is a weapon to make guests leave.

clue.text: Source of notes — on back of envelope, originally

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of each word in the run

explanation.surface: Jotting notes on the back of an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests jottings on scrap paper; it means musical notes from a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument that produces musical tones.

clue.text: Comic is dapper in tight trousers

indicators.note: comic suggests a funny or absurd rearrangement of is, dapper and in

explanation.surface: A comedian looks smart in skinny trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainpipes are very narrow-legged trousers, popular with 1950s Teddy boys.

clue.text: Source of poetry in 18th century or earlier

explanation.surface: Asking about poetry from the 1700s or before.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Prior was an English poet of the early 1700s; prior also means previous.

clue.text: Person who talks when you wish him to listen

definitions.text: Person who talks when you wish him to listen

parts.words: Person who talks when you wish him to listen
parts.note: a cynic's view of a tedious companion as anyone talking when you want to speak

explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome conversationalist, Bierce jokes, is just someone hogging the talk you wanted.

clue.text: Comrade, not PM, I serve

parts.note: AM, morning, is the opposite of PM, afternoon
a serve in tennis is one's go or turn

explanation.surface: A friend declares they are not the Prime Minister but a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' suggests Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used in English for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Unknown's ninety not out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of ninety and not are disordered

explanation.surface: A batsman unknown to fans finishes on ninety not out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ninety not out' is a cricket score: a batsman who has made ninety runs and is still in.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no importance, an unknown.

clue.text: Place of retirement for women who wish for leisure to meditate upon the vice of idleness

definitions.text: Place of retirement for women who wish for leisure to meditate upon the vice of idleness

parts.words: Place of retirement for women who wish for leisure to meditate upon the vice of idleness
parts.note: a cynic's view of a nunnery as a retreat where idle women contemplate the sin of sloth

explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is where women withdraw from the world, which Bierce mocks as a home for idle contemplation.
